scope: Serial CPU reference on the complete native electrical graph; candidate-local optimistic reservations, no distributed grants or hardware implementation.

topology.boundary: complete native membership mask has two or more bits
topology.portal: zero-hop transition inside one boundary electrical node; no extra PIP, occupancy or delay
topology.local_edge: both endpoint memberships contain selected die AND raw physical PIP belongs to that die
topology.eligibility: same qualified CSR, frozen outside footprints, node protection and exclusive net policy as direct cohort

planning.die_path: deterministic multi-source shortest simple die path from existing tree memberships
planning.ranking: minimum tile-box gap from tree seeds plus gap to sink plus current negotiated node cost; a proposal score, not timing or an admissible path bound
planning.repair: ban failed portal and retry within explicit attempt limit
planning.fallback: unchanged full-graph guided sparse search, including routes requiring die reentry

reservation.identity: union of selected electrical portal IDs and any new multi-SLR sink
reservation.shared_tree: existing tree nodes are multi-source seeds; existing shared SLL is counted once per net
reservation.authority_mutation: none during any candidate search; accepted complete branch is published through NativeRouteState.accept
reservation.release: discard entire candidate union on failure, budget/overflow, losing comparison or outer stale replay
reservation.capacity: distinct-net occupancy may be overused during negotiated routing; final convergence requires zero overused nodes. These are not strict concurrent capacity grants.

reentry.trigger: tree already reaches sink die and another die
reentry.comparison: compare complete incremental branch cost, then full depth, attachment, lexicographic path and PIPs
reentry.saved_candidate: no authoritative writes; release saved reservation even if later candidate throws
reentry.scope: bounded deterministic proposals, not a globally optimal hierarchical solver

cost_bound.upper_bound: already found complete candidate cost minus accumulated prefix cost
cost_bound.lower_bound: existing consistent quotient potential to the current segment goal
cost_bound.prune: g+h strictly greater than upper bound; equal-cost alternatives remain eligible
cost_bound.failed_status: cost_limited is distinct from exhausted and resource budget exhausted
cost_bound.repair_effect: a cost-pruned portal may allow another repair attempt; therefore complete run equivalence to the unbounded proposal schedule is not assumed
cost_bound.quotient_work_bound: Reverse quotient BFS stops at min(source distance, C+1); all undiscovered eligible groups are clamped to that distance, including disconnected groups. This keeps labels with g+h <= C identical and also bounds heuristic preparation work.

shadow_integration: same immutable remote boundary overlay and complete decision-read validation; stale plans/paths are discarded and all corridor work reruns against current serial authority
evidence: all completed candidates include directed PIP paths and complete costs; verifier reconstructs accepted trees, occupancy, history, versions, publication snapshots and final drain across epochs
limitations: No physical timing or wirelength model in proposal ranking; PIP count is not physical wirelength.
CPU source-observer boundary overlay still reads centralized local/nonboundary authority.
No die-local concurrent workers, hardware/HBM traffic or board results.
New candidate trees need native DCP connectivity, route/DRC, timing, bus-skew and bitstream checks before signoff claims.

portal_comparison.limits: Both completed nonlocal candidate limit and global attempt limit apply; failed/pruned proposals consume attempts.
portal_comparison.enumeration: Ban the final portal of each completed nonlocal proposal, then replan with the existing ranking. No exhaustive enumeration of upstream portals or die sequences.
portal_comparison.selection: Same complete incremental cost and deterministic tie tuple as reentry comparison; no authority mutation until final selection.
portal_comparison.reentry_composition: If enabled, the zero-transition local extension is evaluated first and does not consume the nonlocal completed-candidate limit.
portal_comparison.bound: Existing incumbent prefix-subtracted cost bound applies to alternative portals; equal cost remains eligible.
portal_comparison.default_compatibility: A limit of one preserves prior first-feasible behavior, including reentry behavior when enabled.
